Change c0395. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. IV; 1831 Ch. XXI.

Context before (unchanged): He walked on first, carrying a part of the fishing tackle, and his companions followed him at some distance.

1818 text: As he was proceeding along the sands, he struck his foot against something, and fell all his length on the ground.

1831 text: As he was proceeding along the sands, he struck his foot against something, and fell at his length on the ground.

Diff: As he was proceeding along the sands, he struck his foot against something, and fell [-all-] {+at+} his length on the ground.

Context after (unchanged): His companions came up to assist him; and, by the light of their lantern, they found that he had fallen on the body of a man, who was to all appearance dead.

result.rationale: Idiomatic phrase swap, 'fell all his length' to 'fell at his length'; same event, same meaning, only minor diction/idiom change with no interpretive consequence.
